subject: PioneerWell — unpacking features for a tier shift and upgrade path
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.j@pioneerwell.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@pioneerwell.com
Date: 2026-11-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick question — moving between tiers and unbundling features

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the call this morning. We're re-evaluating our plan to move several high-throughput routes from our current Compact tier into the Throughput Plus tier for Q1. Two quick asks so we can align internally:

1) Can you confirm which features are gated to Throughput Plus vs available as add-ons to Compact (specifically: per-route priority, KV-cache retention > 24h, and model-variant pinning)?

2) If we upgrade mid-quarter, how do seat counts and prorations work? Do we get any one-time migration credits for the bump?

We have an upcoming procurement review on Nov 10 and it'd help to have an options table + a rough discount range (if applicable) so our CFO can model it.

—Avery
Avery Johnson
Head of Platform, PioneerWell
avery.j@pioneerwell.com
(415) 555-0182

[attachment: PioneerWell_Migration_Workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.j@pioneerwell.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick question — moving between tiers and unbundling features

Hi Avery — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then I'll attach a concise options table.

- Gated features: per-route priority (Throughput Plus only by default), KV-cache retention beyond 24h (Throughput Plus or as a paid add-on to Compact), model-variant pinning (available as an add-on on both tiers but recommended on Throughput Plus for SLA-sensitive routes).

- Mid-quarter upgrades: we prorate at the day level for usage/seat differentials. Migration credits: we typically offer a one-time migration credit for commitments that bump monthly committed throughput by 30%+, subject to deal approval.

I'm looping in Ben (pricing) to put a conservative discount band and confirm the one-time credit policy. Attached is a short options table (summary).

Next steps: Ben to propose numbers; if that looks reasonable, we'll draft an amendment + SOW and I can continue to shepherd through procurement.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
[attachment: options-table-PioneerWell.pdf (summary)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.j@pioneerwell.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick question — moving between tiers and unbundling features

Avery — appreciate the details. High-level pricing options below (numbers are list rates before any concession):

Option A — Full tier upgrade (Compact -> Throughput Plus)
• Committed monthly throughput increases to 3.5M tokens
• Per-token rate: $0.0016
• One-time migration credit: up to $6,000 if commit increases 30%+

Option B — Stay Compact + add-on bundle (priority routing + 48h KV retention + variant pinning)
• Add-on fee (monthly): $2,400
• Per-token rate: $0.0019
• No migration credit (since no tier commitment increase)

Concession guidance: with a 12-month renewal and the current usage profile you shared, we can consider a 10–15% list discount on Option A (secureable after legal review and deal_id PW-2026-089). For a shorter 6-month pilot, we can offer a one-time pilot credit instead of a discount (value: $3,000).

If you can drop the completed migration workbook, I'll run a line-by-line delta to make the pricing proposal final for procurement.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Phone: (650) 555-0109

From: Avery Johnson <avery.j@pioneerwell.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: PioneerWell Procurement <procurement@pioneerwell.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T14:55:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick question — moving between tiers and unbundling features

Thanks Ben — that helps a lot. Attached is the migration workbook with our projected route-level throughput and expected pilot window (Dec–Feb). A few clarifications from procurement:

- They prefer Option A but want the migration credit to be higher if we commit to a 12-month deal (asking if $10k is feasible).
- They also asked whether variant pinning can be limited to three named routes initially rather than an account-wide add-on.

Attaching the workbook and a redlineable SOW draft. Please review and advise by EOD Friday if possible — procurement's internal review is next Monday.

Avery
[attachments: PioneerWell_Migration_Workbook.xlsx, SOW-draft-PW-089.pdf]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.j@pioneerwell.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T10:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick question — moving between tiers and unbundling features

Avery — looping in finance/ops approval. We can support an elevated migration credit of $10,000 on the condition that PioneerWell signs a 12-month committed throughput amendment at the Option A levels Ben proposed.

On the variant pinning ask: we can scope it as a scoped pilot — pin up to three named routes under a named-entities clause in the SOW. If the pilot expands, we'll roll into account-wide entitlements at the agreed add-on rate or the Throughput Plus baseline.

I'll review the SOW redline this afternoon; Soojin, can you prepare the amendment and a clean invoice template so procurement has the numbers to circulate?

Kimberly Park
Director, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
[internal note: approve $10k migration credit for PW-2026-089; require signed 12mo amendment]
